title: Care Level Notices and Effective Dates — Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement
content:
**Article on care level changes.** Under the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement a care level changes only after an assessment and a written level notice.

**1. Written level notice.** Every assessment that indicates a level different from the level billed is followed by a written level notice to the resident and the representative on file, issued no later than the level notice period (2 calendar days) after the assessment date and stating the new level and its effective date.

**2. Increase after a routine or post-move-in reassessment.** An increase found at a routine or post-move-in reassessment takes effect on the notice date plus the level increase notice period (30 calendar days). Such an increase may be recorded only once that period has passed since the written level notice was issued. The notice period is counted in calendar days from the notice date, the notice date being day 0, and the increase takes effect on the day the count reaches 30.

**3. Decrease.** A decrease at any type of reassessment takes effect on the first day of the calendar month following the assessment date.

**4. One change per notice.** A level change is recorded once per level notice, and the level change takes the level stated on the notice it follows.

**5. Prorated care fee.** A prorated care fee is the monthly care fee of the level multiplied by the days billed and divided by the days in the calendar month, rounded to the cent.

**Retired clauses — no longer in force.** The following two clauses are no longer in force and have been superseded by the current basis:
- "An increase found at a change-of-condition or post-hospital reassessment takes effect on the assessment date, because the added care is delivered from that day."
- "When the effective date falls inside a month already billed, the care fee of that month is split at the effective date: the days from the effective date are charged at the new level as a prorated level change charge, and for a decrease the days at the old level from the effective date are returned as a level change proration credit referencing the original care fee charge."

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Event | Date | Consequence under the clauses in force |
|---|---|---|
| Routine reassessment indicates an increase | 3 May | Written notice due no later than 5 May |
| Written notice of that increase issued | 5 May (day 0) | Increase takes effect 4 June (day 30); it may not be recorded on 3 June (day 29) |
| Change-of-condition reassessment indicates a decrease | 17 May | Decrease takes effect 1 June |
| Post-move-in reassessment indicates a decrease | 31 July | Decrease takes effect 1 August |

superseded_clauses: An increase found at a change_of_condition or post_hospital reassessment takes effect on the assessment date, because the added care is delivered from that day.

When the effective date falls inside a month already billed, the care fee of that month is split at the effective date: the days from the effective date are charged at the new level as a prorated_level_change charge, and for a decrease the days at the old level from the effective date are returned as a level_change_proration credit referencing the original care fee charge.
